questions.q: Which body system carries oxygen and nutrients around the body?
questions.fact: The circulatory system includes the heart, blood and blood vessels.

questions.q: Which body system breaks down food into nutrients?
questions.fact: The digestive system includes the mouth, stomach and intestines.

questions.q: Which body system includes the lungs and windpipe?
questions.fact: The respiratory system brings in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which body system removes liquid waste from the blood?
questions.fact: The kidneys filter about 150 liters of blood every day.

questions.q: Which body system includes the skin, hair and nails?
questions.fact: Integument means a covering.

questions.q: About how much does an adult's skin weigh?
questions.fact: That makes skin heavier than any single internal organ.

questions.q: What helps keep skin safe from sunburn?
questions.fact: Sunscreen should be put on again every couple of hours outside.

questions.q: What is the condition called when the body gets dangerously hot?
questions.fact: Rest in the shade, drink water and get help if someone shows signs of heatstroke.

questions.q: What is it called when the body gets dangerously cold?
questions.fact: Shivering is your body's way of making heat by moving muscles quickly.

questions.q: What is frostbite?
choices: Freezing of skin and tissue in extreme cold
A bite from a winter insect
questions.fact: Fingers, toes, ears and noses are most at risk of frostbite.

questions.q: Why do you shiver when you are cold?
questions.fact: Shivering can increase the heat your body makes several times over.

questions.q: Why does your face turn red when you are embarrassed or hot?
choices: Blood vessels near the skin widen
questions.fact: This helps your body release heat.

questions.q: What do your kidneys make from waste and extra water?
questions.fact: Your kidneys clean all your blood many times every day.

questions.q: What is the yellow color in urine from?
choices: A substance made when old red blood cells break down
questions.fact: Drinking more water makes urine lighter in color.

questions.q: What does the gallbladder store?
questions.fact: People can live without a gallbladder.

questions.q: What organ do you use to think?
questions.fact: Ancient Egyptians thought the heart did the thinking and threw away the brain during mummification.

questions.q: Can you live without your appendix?
choices: Only if you are an adult
questions.fact: Scientists think the appendix may store helpful gut bacteria.

questions.q: How many lungs do people have?
questions.fact: Together, your lungs have a surface area about the size of half a tennis court.

questions.q: About how many breaths does a resting adult take per minute?
questions.fact: Kids usually breathe a bit faster than adults.

questions.q: What happens to your heart rate when you exercise?
questions.fact: Exercise makes your heart stronger over time.

questions.q: Why is regular exercise good for your body?
choices: It strengthens your heart, lungs, muscles and bones
It stops you from needing sleep
questions.fact: Kids should aim for about an hour of active play every day.

questions.q: What happens to muscles when you exercise them often?
questions.fact: Tiny tears in muscle fibers repair and grow back stronger.

questions.q: What causes the sore feeling in muscles a day or two after hard exercise?
choices: Tiny muscle fiber damage being repaired
questions.fact: Soreness usually goes away in a few days.

questions.q: What is a cramp?
choices: A sudden, painful tightening of a muscle
questions.fact: Stretching the muscle gently can help a cramp go away.

questions.q: What is the heel bone called?
questions.fact: The heel bone is the largest bone in the foot.

questions.q: How many bones are in one human foot?
questions.fact: Your two feet together have 52 bones, about a quarter of all your bones.

questions.q: What is the arch of your foot for?
choices: Absorbing shock and helping you walk
questions.fact: The arch acts like a spring with every step.

questions.q: What are the tough, thick patches of skin that form from rubbing called?
questions.fact: Guitar players often get calluses on their fingertips.

questions.q: What is a blister?
choices: A bubble of fluid under the skin from rubbing or burns
questions.fact: The fluid protects the skin underneath while it heals.

questions.q: What is the white part of your eye called?
questions.fact: The sclera is tough and helps protect the eye.

questions.q: What is the part of the eye that focuses light onto the retina?
questions.fact: As people get older, the lens gets stiffer, so many need reading glasses.

questions.q: What is a cataract?
choices: A big waterfall in the eye
A cloudy lens in the eye
questions.fact: Cataracts can be fixed by replacing the lens with an artificial one.

questions.q: What do eyelashes do?
choices: Keep dust and dirt out of your eyes
questions.fact: Eyelashes fall out and grow back every few months.

questions.q: What are eyebrows good for?
choices: Keeping sweat and rain out of your eyes
questions.fact: Eyebrows also help show feelings like surprise or anger.

questions.q: What is your nose's sense of smell called?
questions.fact: The smell sensors are in a small patch high inside your nose.

questions.q: What do the tiny hairs inside your nose do?
questions.fact: Mucus also traps dirt so it does not reach your lungs.

questions.q: What is the outer part of your ear that you can see called?
questions.fact: The pinna is shaped to funnel sound into your ear canal.

questions.q: What is the sense of taste called in science?
questions.fact: Your taste buds are mostly on the tiny bumps on your tongue, called papillae.

questions.q: What kind of doctor takes care of children?
questions.fact: Pediatric comes from a Greek word for child.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in the heart?
questions.fact: Cardio comes from the Greek word for heart.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in skin?
questions.fact: Dermatologists help with rashes, acne and checking moles.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in the brain and nerves?
questions.fact: Neuro comes from the Greek word for nerve.

questions.q: What kind of dentist straightens teeth with braces?
questions.fact: Ortho means straight in Greek.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in feet?
questions.fact: Pod comes from the Greek word for foot.

questions.q: What machine uses strong magnets to take detailed pictures inside the body?
questions.fact: MRI stands for magnetic resonance imaging.

questions.q: What do doctors use to look inside your ears?
questions.fact: Oto comes from the Greek word for ear.

questions.q: What is a cast used for?
choices: Holding a broken bone still while it heals
questions.fact: Broken bones in kids often heal in about four to eight weeks.

questions.q: Which ancient Greek doctor is called the father of medicine?
questions.fact: Many new doctors still take an oath named after him.

questions.q: Who is known as the founder of modern nursing?
questions.fact: She was called the Lady with the Lamp because she checked on soldiers at night.

questions.q: In what year did the first successful human heart transplant happen?
questions.fact: Surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed it in South Africa.

questions.q: What do we call a doctor who performs operations?
questions.fact: Surgeons wear masks and gloves to keep germs out of the patient's body.

questions.q: What is an X-ray mostly used to look at?
questions.fact: Bones block X-rays and show up white on the picture.

questions.q: What do you call medicine that kills bacteria?
questions.fact: Taking the whole course of antibiotics, as a doctor says, helps stop bacteria from coming back.

questions.q: What is first aid?
choices: Basic care given right away to someone hurt or sick
The first patient of the day
questions.fact: Knowing simple first aid can help in an emergency before help arrives.

questions.q: What should you do first for a small cut?
questions.fact: Then cover it with a clean bandage.

questions.q: What should you do for a minor burn?
choices: Put ice directly on it for an hour
Cool it under cool running water
questions.fact: Butter and ice can actually make burns worse.

questions.q: What should you do if someone is choking and cannot breathe or talk?
choices: Get help and give abdominal thrusts if trained
Make them lie down and sleep
questions.fact: Abdominal thrusts are also called the Heimlich maneuver.

questions.q: What number do you call for emergencies in the United States?
questions.fact: In the United Kingdom it is 999, and in much of Europe it is 112.

questions.q: What is CPR used for?
choices: Helping someone whose heart has stopped
questions.fact: CPR stands for cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

questions.q: What is a nosebleed?
choices: A sign of a cold only
Bleeding from tiny blood vessels inside the nose
questions.fact: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of your nose to stop a nosebleed.

questions.q: What is a concussion?
choices: A brain injury from a hit to the head
questions.fact: Wearing a helmet for biking and skating helps protect your brain.

questions.q: Why should you wear a helmet when biking?
choices: To protect your brain if you fall
questions.fact: Helmets greatly lower the chance of serious head injury in a crash.

questions.q: Why should you not look at screens right before bed?
choices: Bright light can make it harder to fall asleep
Screens make your eyes change color
It makes you grow slower overnight
questions.fact: Blue-rich light from screens can lower melatonin, the sleep hormone.

questions.q: What is the voice box's pair of folds that vibrate to make sound?
questions.fact: Vocal cords get longer and thicker during the teen years, which deepens voices.

questions.q: Why does your voice sound different on a recording?
choices: Your ears are blocked when you talk
You usually hear your voice through your bones too
questions.fact: Sound traveling through your skull makes your voice seem deeper to you.

questions.q: What part of the body makes up your Adam's apple?
questions.fact: Everyone has one, but it often sticks out more after puberty.

questions.q: What is the fastest-healing part of the body?
questions.fact: Mouth cuts often heal in just a few days.

questions.q: What is the strongest bone in the body?
questions.fact: The femur can support about 30 times the weight of your body.

questions.q: What percentage of your body weight is your skeleton, roughly?
questions.fact: Bones are light for how strong they are, because they are partly hollow and full of marrow.

questions.q: How many senses do people usually say we have?
questions.fact: Scientists say there are actually many more, like balance and temperature.

questions.q: What are the five classic senses?
choices: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch
Sight, sound, sleep, speech and smile
Hearing, walking, eating, seeing and talking
Taste, color, music, smell and heat
questions.fact: Each sense sends signals to a different part of the brain.

questions.q: What part of the brain handles vision?
choices: The frontal lobe at the front
The occipital lobe at the back
questions.fact: That is why a hard hit to the back of the head can make you see stars.

questions.q: What part of the brain helps with planning and decision-making?
questions.fact: The frontal lobe keeps developing until people are in their twenties.

questions.q: What is the space between the two halves of the brain connected by?
questions.fact: This thick band of nerves lets the left and right halves share information.

questions.q: What is short-term memory?
choices: Holding information for a short time, like a phone number
questions.fact: Most people can hold about seven things in short-term memory at once.

questions.q: What is muscle memory?
choices: Getting better at movements through practice
questions.fact: Practice builds brain pathways that make movements like riding a bike automatic.

questions.q: Which hand do about 90 percent of people prefer to write with?
questions.fact: About 1 in 10 people is left-handed.

questions.q: What is it called when someone can use both hands equally well?
questions.fact: True ambidexterity is quite rare.

questions.q: What is double-jointed really?
choices: Having two joints in one place
questions.fact: Doctors call it hypermobility.

questions.q: What is the dimple in your upper lip under your nose called?
questions.fact: Everyone has a philtrum, and scientists are still not sure if it has a purpose.

questions.q: What is the wall that divides the two nostrils called?
questions.fact: The septum is made of cartilage and bone.

questions.q: What is the belly button's medical name?
questions.fact: It marks where the umbilical cord was attached before you were born.

questions.q: What are the colored rings or patterns in your iris unique like?
questions.fact: Some security systems scan people's irises to identify them.

questions.q: What determines your eye color?
choices: How much melanin is in your iris
questions.fact: Brown is the most common eye color in the world.

questions.q: What is the most common eye color in the world?
questions.fact: Green is one of the rarest eye colors.

questions.q: Why do many babies' eyes change color in their first year?
choices: Melanin builds up in the iris over time
questions.fact: Many babies born with blue eyes end up with brown or green eyes.

questions.q: What is a mole on the skin?
choices: A small animal under the skin
A small cluster of pigment cells
questions.fact: It is good to show a doctor any mole that changes shape, size or color.

questions.q: What is acne?
questions.fact: Acne is very common during the teen years.

questions.q: What is dandruff?
choices: Flakes of dead skin from the scalp
questions.fact: Dandruff is not caused by being dirty.

questions.q: What are head lice?
choices: Tiny insects that live in hair and feed on blood from the scalp
questions.fact: Lice cannot fly or jump, they crawl from head to head.

questions.q: What is athlete's foot?
choices: A sports injury to the ankle
A fungus infection of the skin on the feet
questions.fact: Keeping feet dry and changing socks helps prevent it.

questions.q: What are warts caused by?
questions.fact: Touching a toad does not give you warts.

questions.q: What is asthma?
choices: A condition where the airways swell and narrow, making breathing hard
questions.fact: Many people with asthma use an inhaler to open their airways.

questions.q: What is diabetes?
choices: A condition where the body has trouble controlling blood sugar
questions.fact: Insulin helps sugar move from the blood into cells for energy.

questions.q: Which scientists first used insulin to treat diabetes in 1922?
questions.fact: Before insulin, type 1 diabetes was almost always deadly.

questions.q: What does a pacemaker do?
choices: Helps the heart keep a steady beat
questions.fact: A pacemaker is a small device placed under the skin.

questions.q: What is an organ donor?
choices: Someone who gives an organ to help another person
questions.fact: One donor can save several lives.

questions.q: What is the main job of the skin?
choices: Protecting the body from germs, sun and water loss
questions.fact: Skin also helps control body temperature through sweating.

questions.q: What part of the skin makes oil to keep it soft?
questions.fact: The scientific name is sebaceous glands.

questions.q: How often does your body replace the outer layer of skin?
questions.fact: New skin cells form deep in the epidermis and slowly move up to the surface.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny openings in the skin where sweat comes out?
questions.fact: You have millions of sweat pores over your body.

questions.q: What helps you grip things with your fingertips?
questions.fact: The ridges may also help you feel textures better.

questions.q: What does saliva contain that starts breaking down starch?
questions.fact: If you chew a cracker for a long time, it starts to taste sweeter because starch turns into sugar.

questions.q: About how big is an empty stomach?
choices: About the size of a pea
About the size of a fist
About the size of a basketball
About the size of a car
questions.fact: The stomach can stretch to hold about 1 to 1.5 liters of food.

questions.q: What is the ring of muscle that keeps stomach acid out of the esophagus?
questions.fact: When it does not close well, acid can rise and cause heartburn.

questions.q: What is heartburn?
choices: Stomach acid rising into the esophagus
Eating spicy food in the heart
questions.fact: Despite its name, heartburn has nothing to do with the heart.

questions.q: What does burping release?
choices: Swallowed air and gas from the stomach
questions.fact: Fizzy drinks make people burp because of the gas in them.

questions.q: Which body system includes lymph nodes and lymph vessels?
questions.fact: The lymphatic system carries fluid and helps fight infections.

questions.q: How many kidneys do most people have?
questions.fact: Kidneys sit near your back, just under your ribs.

questions.q: What are the tiny filtering units in your kidneys called?
questions.fact: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.

questions.q: Which organs help control the amount of water in your body?
questions.fact: When you drink a lot, your kidneys make more urine.

questions.q: Why do you need to go to the bathroom more when it is cold?
choices: Your body sends more fluid to the kidneys
questions.fact: When blood vessels in your skin tighten to save heat, more fluid goes to the kidneys.

questions.q: What is the growth spurt that happens to many kids as they become teenagers part of?
questions.fact: Growth plates near the ends of bones allow kids to grow taller.

questions.q: What are the areas near the ends of kids' long bones where growth happens called?
questions.fact: Growth plates close in the late teens, and then you stop getting taller.

questions.q: Are you taller in the morning or at night?
questions.fact: During the day, the cushions between your vertebrae get squeezed a little.

questions.q: What are the cushions between the bones of the spine called?
questions.fact: Discs act like shock absorbers when you walk, run and jump.

questions.q: What is it called when someone's spine curves sideways?
questions.fact: Doctors often check kids' backs for scoliosis because it can appear during growth spurts.

questions.q: What is arthritis?
choices: Pain and swelling in the joints
questions.fact: Arthritis is more common in older people, but kids can get it too.

questions.q: What are the two main tubes that branch from the windpipe into the lungs called?
questions.fact: They keep branching into smaller tubes like an upside-down tree.

questions.q: Why is smoking harmful to the lungs?
choices: It damages lung tissue and can cause diseases like cancer
It is only harmful to teeth
questions.fact: Lungs can slowly heal after someone stops smoking.

questions.q: Why do you breathe faster when you exercise?
questions.fact: Your heart beats faster too, to deliver the oxygen.

questions.q: What does the word cardio mean?
questions.fact: Cardio exercise, like running and swimming, makes your heart stronger.

questions.q: What sound does your heart make through a stethoscope?
questions.fact: The two sounds come from two sets of valves closing.

questions.q: How long does it take blood to travel around your whole body?
questions.fact: At rest, your heart pumps about 5 liters of blood a minute.

questions.q: What carries messages through your body in the nervous system?
questions.fact: Neurons pass signals using tiny pulses of electricity and chemicals.

questions.q: What is the gap between two nerve cells called?
questions.fact: Chemical messengers jump across the synapse to pass on a signal.

questions.q: What is the long tail of a nerve cell that carries signals away called?
questions.fact: Some axons are covered in a fatty layer that makes signals travel faster.

questions.q: What are the two main parts of the nervous system?
questions.fact: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.q: What do pain signals help you do?
questions.fact: People who cannot feel pain often get hurt without noticing.

questions.q: What is the name of the thin tubes that carry tears from your eyes into your nose?
questions.fact: That is why your nose runs when you cry.

questions.q: What are the air-filled spaces in the bones around your nose called?
questions.fact: When sinuses get swollen during a cold, your face can feel stuffy and sore.

questions.q: What are the two lower chambers of the heart called?
questions.fact: The two upper chambers are called atria.

questions.q: What are the two upper chambers of the heart called?
questions.fact: Blood flows into the atria and then down into the ventricles.

questions.q: Which blood vessel brings blood from the body back into the heart?
questions.fact: The vena cava is the largest vein in the body.

questions.q: What are the arteries in your neck that carry blood to your brain called?
questions.fact: You can feel a pulse in your neck from the carotid arteries.

questions.q: What are the blood vessels that feed the heart muscle itself called?
questions.fact: When a coronary artery gets blocked, it can cause a heart attack.

questions.q: What is a heart attack?
choices: When the heart is broken by sadness
When the heart beats too slowly for fun
When the heart moves to the other side
When blood flow to part of the heart muscle is blocked
questions.fact: Calling emergency services right away is very important during a heart attack.

questions.q: About how much of your blood is made of red blood cells?
questions.fact: Doctors call this percentage the hematocrit.

questions.q: Which are the most common cells in your blood?
questions.fact: There are millions of red blood cells in a single tiny drop of blood.

questions.q: What shape is a red blood cell?
choices: A disc dented in the middle on both sides
questions.fact: This shape gives it lots of surface area to carry oxygen and lets it bend through tiny vessels.

questions.q: What do red blood cells lack that most other cells have?
questions.fact: Without a nucleus, there is more room to carry oxygen.

questions.q: What is it called when white blood cells eat germs?
questions.fact: Phagocytosis means cell eating.

questions.q: What is inflammation?
choices: Redness, heat and swelling as the body fights injury or germs
questions.fact: Inflammation is a sign that your immune system is at work.

questions.q: Why do cuts sometimes get swollen and red?
choices: Extra blood brings in immune cells to fight germs
questions.fact: If redness spreads or it gets very painful, a doctor should check it.

questions.q: What is pus?
choices: Dead white blood cells and germs from an infection
questions.fact: Pus is a sign that your body has been fighting bacteria.

questions.q: What does a vaccine usually contain?
choices: Live, dangerous germs at full strength
A harmless piece or weakened form of a germ
questions.fact: It lets your body practice fighting a germ safely.

questions.q: What is herd immunity?
choices: When you are immune to animals
When a group gets sick together
When enough people are immune that a disease cannot spread easily
questions.fact: It helps protect babies and people who cannot get certain vaccines.

questions.q: What do we call a disease that spreads from person to person?
questions.fact: Colds, flu and chickenpox are contagious diseases.

questions.q: What is a disease spreading around the whole world at once called?
questions.fact: The COVID-19 pandemic began in late 2019.

questions.q: What does a thermometer in a doctor's office measure?
questions.fact: Some thermometers measure temperature in the ear or on the forehead.

questions.q: Which joint is the largest in the human body?
questions.fact: The knee joins the femur, tibia and kneecap.

questions.q: Which joint in the body can move the most freely?
questions.fact: Because it moves so freely, the shoulder is also the joint that dislocates most often.

questions.q: What is a dislocation?
choices: When a bone pops out of its joint
questions.fact: A doctor can usually pop the bone back into place.

questions.q: What is the fluid in joints that keeps them moving smoothly?
questions.fact: It works like oil in a machine's hinges.

questions.q: What is the cracking sound when you crack your knuckles?
questions.fact: Studies have not found that knuckle cracking causes arthritis.

questions.q: Which part of the body contains about 22 bones fused or joined together?
questions.fact: Only one of these bones, the lower jaw, can move.

questions.q: What is the largest bone in the face?
questions.fact: The lower jaw, or mandible, is also the strongest bone in the face.

questions.q: What is the outer covering of a bone called?
questions.fact: The periosteum has nerves, which is why breaking a bone hurts so much.

questions.q: What is the spongy part inside the ends of long bones called?
questions.fact: Spongy bone is light but strong, like a honeycomb.

questions.q: What do we call bone tissue that is hard, dense and on the outside of bones?
questions.fact: Compact bone makes up most of the weight of your skeleton.

questions.q: Which vitamin and mineral together help build strong bones?
questions.fact: Weight-bearing exercise like running and jumping also helps make bones stronger.

questions.q: What happens to your bones when you jump and run often?
questions.fact: Bones respond to stress by adding more bone tissue.

questions.q: Which muscle lets you close your eyelids?
questions.fact: This ring-shaped muscle surrounds each eye.

questions.q: Which is the longest muscle in the human body?
questions.fact: The sartorius runs across the front of the thigh from the hip to the knee.

questions.q: Which is the smallest muscle in the human body?
questions.fact: The stapedius is in the middle ear and is only about 1 millimeter long.

questions.q: What is the tongue made of?
questions.fact: The tongue's muscles let it change shape for talking, eating and swallowing.

questions.q: What is unique about each person's tongue?
choices: It can taste only one flavor
Its print is unique, like a fingerprint
questions.fact: Scientists have studied tongue prints as a way to identify people.

questions.q: What happens to the pupils of your eyes in a dark room?
questions.fact: Bigger pupils let in more light so you can see better in the dark.

questions.q: How long does it take your eyes to fully adjust to the dark?
questions.fact: That is why astronomers avoid bright lights before stargazing.

questions.q: Why do some people need glasses to read as they get older?
choices: The lens of the eye gets stiffer
questions.fact: This condition is called presbyopia.

questions.q: What is the medical name for being nearsighted?
questions.fact: Spending time outdoors in daylight may help lower kids' chances of becoming nearsighted.

questions.q: What is the name for a blurry vision problem caused by an unevenly curved cornea?
questions.fact: Glasses or contact lenses can correct astigmatism.

questions.q: What is the special alphabet of raised dots that lets blind people read by touch?
questions.fact: Louis Braille invented it in the 1820s when he was a teenager.

questions.q: What is the language that uses hand shapes and movements, used by many deaf people?
questions.fact: There are many sign languages around the world, like American Sign Language and British Sign Language.

questions.q: What device helps some people with hearing loss hear better?
questions.fact: A cochlear implant is another device that can help people who are deeply deaf.

questions.q: What happens to your hearing if you listen to very loud music for a long time?
questions.fact: Keeping headphone volume at a moderate level helps protect your hearing.

questions.q: What is the name of the clear jelly that fills most of the eyeball?
questions.fact: Tiny clumps in this jelly cast shadows on the retina that look like floating specks, called floaters.

questions.q: What do you call the small, round muscle at the bottom of the stomach that lets food into the small intestine?
questions.fact: It opens a little at a time so food moves out of the stomach slowly.

questions.q: What is the main job of the large blood vessel called the pulmonary artery?
choices: Carrying blood from the heart to the lungs
questions.fact: Unlike most arteries, it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.q: What is the body's natural painkiller chemical, released during exercise?
questions.fact: Endorphins can give people a happy feeling after a good workout.

questions.q: Which chemical messenger helps you feel happy and calm and is made mostly in your gut?
questions.fact: Most of the body's serotonin is actually made in the digestive system.

questions.q: What is the stress hormone your body makes when you are under pressure?
questions.fact: Short bursts of cortisol help you focus, but too much stress for too long is not healthy.
